## What Is an Employer of Record in Kazakhstan


Hiring in Kazakhstan without a local entity used to mean two choices: skip the market or spend months setting one up. An Employer of Record (EOR) removes that tradeoff. An EOR is a third-party organization that becomes the legal employer of your Kazakhstan hire on paper, signing the local employment contract and handling the statutory filings that come with it, while your company runs the relationship day to day.


This split separates legal responsibility from management responsibility. As explained in our[employer of record explainer](https://www.bolto.com/blog/eor-definition-employer-of-record) , the EOR owns the employment contract, payroll withholding, tax registration, and ongoing compliance with Kazakhstan’s labor code. You stay the day-to-day employer: assigning work, setting goals, and running performance reviews just as you would with any other team member.


For a single hire or a small team in Kazakhstan, standing up a local entity rarely makes sense. Entity registration and the corporate compliance obligations that follow it suit companies planning a long-term local presence, not those making one hire. An[employer of record](https://www.bolto.com/global-hr) lets you skip that setup while keeping the employment compliant with Kazakhstan’s labor law from day one.


## Employment Laws and Compliance Requirements in Kazakhstan


Kazakhstan’s labor code sets out specific requirements for how an employment relationship has to be structured, and getting these details right matters whether you’re hiring through an EOR or standing up your own entity. Employers generally need a[written employment contract](https://www.adilet.zan.kz/eng/docs/K1500000414) from day one, along with registration for[mandatory social contributions](https://taxsummaries.pwc.com/kazakhstan/individual/other-taxes) that fund pension, medical, and social insurance programs. Under Kazakhstan’s labor code, statutory annual paid leave is generally 24 calendar days, and the standard notice period for termination is typically one month, though both figures can shift depending on contract terms and how regulations are updated. Missing a filing deadline or misjudging a notice period can expose a company to back payments, disputes, or compliance penalties, even when the mistake was unintentional. This is general information, not legal advice. Rules vary by situation and change over time, so consult a qualified employment lawyer for your specific circumstances before finalizing contract terms in Kazakhstan.

## EOR vs. Local Entity in Kazakhstan: Which Is Right for You


Choosing between an EOR and a local entity in Kazakhstan comes down to how committed you are to a long-term, large-scale presence there. An EOR makes sense when you’re hiring one person or a small team, want to move fast, and don’t want ongoing legal and accounting overhead sitting on your books. A local entity starts to pay off once you’re hiring a larger, long-term team, since the fixed costs of incorporation and compliance upkeep get spread across more employees and you gain full control over benefits design and equity administration. The tradeoff: an EOR gets you compliant and hiring within days, while a local entity can take weeks to months to stand up and carries a slower, costlier exit if you ever need to wind it down. For most founders making their first hire in Kazakhstan, the EOR path removes the setup burden without sacrificing compliance, letting you test the market before committing to the heavier infrastructure a local entity requires.


### Choose an EOR if


- You're hiring one person or a small team in Kazakhstan and don't want to commit to a full local entity just to get started
- You need to move fast, since an EOR gets a hire signed, onboarded, and compliant within days instead of months
- You'd rather keep legal and accounting overhead off your books while you test the Kazakhstan market
- You want a straightforward exit if your plans in Kazakhstan change, since EOR offboarding is simpler than a formal entity dissolution


### Choose a Local Entity if


- You're building a larger, long-term team in Kazakhstan, where fixed incorporation and compliance costs get spread across more employees
- You want full control over benefits design and equity administration beyond what a standard EOR arrangement typically allows
- You're committed to a long-term presence in the market and can absorb the weeks-to-months setup timeline
- You have the internal legal and accounting resources to manage Kazakhstan's ongoing compliance upkeep directly

With an EOR, you pay for the employee relationship instead of entity overhead, which keeps costs lower for a single hire.
